A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same study. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable matching across pagination changes. v1 has no appendix; v2 adds an accessible Appendix A.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 2–8 report original Monte Carlo fault-injection experiments, architectural ablations and LUT layer-parity recovery results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original fault-injection experiments and additionally reports training runtime and model storage in Appendix A, Table 3.

M1.justification: The sparse Boolean LUT architecture, Extended Finite Difference training and popcount classification head remain unchanged. Added motivation and experimental details do not introduce a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, Google Speech Commands keyword spotting and ToyAdmos anomaly detection under the same corruption scenarios. Larger CNNs, Transformers and foundation models appear only in discussion, not new evaluations.

E2.justification: Figures 2 and 7 retain their respective comparator sets. v2 explicitly identifies Figure 7's FP32, FP16, FP8 and BNN curves as CNN baselines, already described in v1 Section 5.1. Table 3 compares existing model variants.

E3.justification: Appendix A extends evaluation to average training runtime and inference-parameter storage, explicitly including affine-quantization metadata. Existing fault-injection sweeps and ablation ranges are retained; the newly specified default MLP configuration is additional documentation.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a supplementary resource-cost comparison, examining training time and storage across the retained model variants. The existing precision, width, depth, activation, sparsity and layer-parity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify approximately 100 Monte Carlo trials per point. v2 introduces no new seed information, uncertainty-reporting procedure, confidence-interval definition or significance test.

E6.justification: Figure 7 revises weighted-baseline clean accuracies and BNN curves, while the LUT curve remains unchanged; for example, plotted KWS BNN accuracy at p = 0.05 changes from roughly 0.24 to 0.34. Table 3 adds resource results, including 8 versus 10 minutes average training time for FP32 and Logic/LUT, and MNIST storage of 795 versus 6 KiB. The main resilience findings persist.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–10, Corollaries 1–2 and their mathematical derivations are retained. Added explanations of the independent-bit model and Equation 22 clarify applicability and meaning without changing formal assumptions, formulas or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about structural resilience, favorable architectural factors, LUT robustness and even-layer recovery. Added explanations and resource measurements do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4.1 add specific limitations concerning replacement of large CNNs/Transformers by pure LUT models and applicability to correlated hardware faults. Section 5.2 adds a concrete discussion of the clean-accuracy versus resilience trade-off using KWS.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the default ablation model as an FP32, one-hidden-layer MLP with 256 hidden neurons and ReLU. Appendix A adds NVIDIA A100 hardware information, training times and inference-storage accounting. These disclosures do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a focused expressivity, efficiency and scalability discussion, citing VC-dimension analysis and recent systems including AMIGOLUT, NeuraLUT-Assemble and differentiable weightless controllers. This expands the literature context while retaining the original resilience-focused positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds targeted explanatory paragraphs, acknowledgements and Appendix A, and corrects several citation constructions. The main section order, argument structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3, publication headers and a review-information line, and reflows existing figures, notably placing Figure 8 on the conclusion page. Existing plot structures, legends and captions, and Tables 1–2, are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through explicit ablation defaults and resource reporting, and improves interpretation through specific hardware-fault and scalability limitations. The expanded literature discussion also provides useful context. These gains are limited: the theoretical core and experimental coverage remain unchanged, and the reason for Figure 7's revised baseline values is unexplained.
